fixes.explanation: That's it. Amos says the pastures of the shepherds mourn, and the summit of Carmel withers. So when the LORD roars, the land feels it. Even the grass is not having a good day, and Amos is a sheepherder, so I think those pastures matter to him.

Yes, baker. The LORD says, "I will cut off the ruler from the Valley of Aven and the one who wields the scepter in Beth-eden." Those rulers are in charge now, and the LORD says they'll be cut off. He also says He will break down the gates of Damascus.
Right, baker. The verse says, "The people of Aram will be exiled to Kir…" says the LORD. They don't get to stay in their land. It's a heavy line, and I think it's hard to read.

Nice guess, friend, but treasures aren't what the verse says. The LORD says Tyre delivered up a whole congregation of exiles to Edom. It's people again, and not a single treasure chest is in the charge.

No chariots in this verse, baker. The LORD says Tyre delivered up a whole congregation of exiles to Edom. The charge is about people being handed over, not gear. Horses would have been an easier charge to hear, I think.

You got it. The LORD says Tyre delivered up exiles to Edom "…and broke a covenant of brotherhood." So the charge has two parts, and the second is about a covenant Tyre broke. A covenant is a serious promise, and the LORD names this one as a covenant of brotherhood.

Not quite, friend. The LORD says Edom's "…anger raged continually, and his fury flamed incessantly." That is not a flare-up that cooled off. It's anger that kept going, and the LORD says Edom stifled all compassion too.

That's right. The LORD says they did it "…in order to enlarge their territory." It's one of the heaviest lines in the whole passage. I think this one hurts to read. The LORD names the reason, and it was about land.

Moab gets its own charge a bit later, baker, and it's a different one. For the Ammonites, the LORD says they did it in order to enlarge their territory. This is one of the heavy parts of the passage. The reason is in the verse.

Keeping a throne isn't in this verse, baker. The LORD says the Ammonite king will go into exile with his princes together. A throne is hard to keep from another country. The verse gives exile, not a surrender.

Yes, friend. The LORD says Moab "…burned to lime the bones of Edom’s king." It's a hard charge. It's also a reminder that Edom shows up in this passage as a nation with a charge, and also as someone who was wronged.
The verse says otherwise, baker. The LORD says, “…he burned to lime the bones of Edom’s king.” It's a hard charge. Moab did this to a king of Edom, and the LORD names it.

Prophets feel like a good guess, friend, especially with Amos talking. But the LORD's charge says Judah rejects the Law of the LORD and fails to keep His statutes. The Law is what's named in the verse. Prophets aren't mentioned in the charge.

A king isn't named in this charge, friend. The LORD says Judah is led astray by the lies in which their fathers walked. That points to their fathers walking in those lies, so it reaches back before this king. The verse doesn't say anything about the king's part.
